description: Remove every hardcoded self-binary-name dependency from the code: auto-spawn resolves by execPath, process discovery stops comparing argv against a single name literal, and the self-invoke helper drops its own literal fallback.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.spawn/Bun.spawnSync take `command: string[]` and use posix_spawn(3); cmd[0] is an executable path or name, so passing an absolute `process.execPath` is fully supported and needs no PATH lookup. An `argv0` option exists to override the argv[0] the child advertises, which is what other processes (and `ps -eo pid,args`) observe. No breaking changes or deprecations affecting this cycle.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: Bun exposes `argv0` as a way to keep advertising a fixed name to `ps`, which would preserve stop.ts's current literal-name discovery; the local convention (execPath self-invoke, src/util/self-invoke.ts) instead makes the advertised argv0 vary by install path, so discovery must become name-agnostic rather than being pinned back with argv0.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: isSidecarArgv over-matches and makes `cam stop` SIGTERM unrelated pro…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [src/commands/stop.ts:298]: isSidecarArgv over-matches and makes `cam stop` SIGTERM unrelated processes. The predicate accepts ANY argv of length 2 or 3 whose last token is the literal word 'sidecar', so any command running in the project cwd that happens to end in that word is classified as this project's sidecar and sent SIGTERM by the fallback scan (performStop step 1c, stop.ts:481-491). Proven at Layer B against the REAL production path (real `ps -eo pid,args` + real `lsof` via defaultListProcesses, killFn stubbed to record only): `Bun.spawn(['/usr/bin/tail','-F','sidecar'], {cwd})` yielded fallbackSidecarKilled=true and killFn received the tail's pid 58293 (see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3). Realistic collisions in a dev cwd: `rg sidecar`, `tail -F sidecar`, `git log sidecar`. This is a regression: main anchored the match on record.argv[0] === 'cam', so no unrelated command could match. It also defeats the intent of US-004 acceptance criterion 2 case 4 ('a process in the project cwd that is not running the sidecar subcommand does NOT match'): the chosen fixture ['bun','/repo/index.ts','run'] passes while the whole false-positive class stays open. Fix by keeping name-agnosticism but re-anchoring on a property the real self-spawn always has and an ad-hoc command does not, e.g. require argv[0] to be an absolute executable path (both production shapes, [execPath,'sidecar'] and [runtime,script,'sidecar'], always carry one because Bun.spawn is handed process.execPath), and add a negative test for the ['tail','-F','sidecar'] / ['rg','sidecar'] class.

userStories.title: WARNING: The same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose executable path…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/stop.ts:336]: The same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose executable path contains a space. defaultListProcesses splits the `ps` args column with `argsStr.split(/\s+/)`, and isSidecarArgv requires exactly 2 or 3 tokens; before this branch argv[0] was always the bare literal 'cam' so token count was stable, but US-002 now puts the full absolute execPath (and, interpreted, the full script path) into the ps line. An install under e.g. `/Users/x/My Tools/cam` produces 3+ tokens for the compiled shape and 4+ for the interpreted one, so the live sidecar becomes invisible to the fallback scan and `cam stop` silently leaves it running. The diff itself treats space-bearing paths as in-scope (test/integration/dashboard-pane-selfspawn.test.ts:74-76 deliberately uses 'cam script dir/run me.ts'), so the ps parser should tolerate them too (e.g. anchor on the last token plus an absolute-path prefix rather than an exact token count).

userStories.description: As the loop driver, I need resolveSelfInvokeArgv to never emit a hardcoded product name, so that every self-spawn built on it resolves to the exact executable currently running instead of whatever the PATH happens to hold.
acceptanceCriteria: resolveSelfInvokeArgv carries no literal binary name, in the returned argv or in its docstring. [oracle: bash -c '! grep -qE "argv1 \?\? .cam." src/util/self-invoke.ts']

The degenerate interpreted-mode case (argv1 undefined) resolves to an execPath-only argv, the helper docstring states that shape, and the existing unit case for the old PATH-lookup fallback is rewritten to assert it. [oracle: bash -c '! grep -q "falls back to the bare" test/util/self-invoke.test.ts']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test), including the two existing production call sites of the helper (src/retry/launcher.ts and src/commands/run.ts via resolveOrchResolverCmd). [oracle: bun test]
The quality spine passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]

Callers spread the returned array, so a shorter argv is safe: src/retry/launcher.ts:242 and src/commands/run.ts:284 (resolveOrchResolverCmd). This story is the foundation the three following ones build on. Bun docs (fetched this cycle): Bun.spawn's cmd[0] may be an absolute executable path, so no PATH-resolvable name is needed anywhere. Keep the pins green: this story must not touch package.json and must not rename CAM_, .cam-, the tmux -L socket, or any /cam- slash command.

GOTCHA (from the issue): discovery inspects OTHER processes' argv, so it cannot just use its own execPath: a legitimate sidecar may be the ALREADY-INSTALLED binary under today's name, or (after US-002) an interpreted `<bun> <script> sidecar`, so the fixed argv[1] === 'sidecar' index assumption breaks too. Recognize the sidecar by its subcommand position in the argv rather than by a name comparison, while keeping the cwd-equality scoping that stops one project killing another's sidecar. The `ps` quick filter exists only to avoid an lsof call per process, so it may relax but must not become unbounded (do not lsof every process on the machine). Existing DI seams to reuse: listProcessesFn / ProcessRecord in stop.ts and the sidecarPidReader family (patterns.md, sidecar PID persistence bullet). Existing coverage lives in test/stop.test.ts; the new file is additive and must be swept red against main before it is trusted.

findings.text: Under-match regression, carried unfixed from round 3 and re-verified live at Layer B this round. `makeSpawnSidecarFn` respawns the sidecar with `stdio: ['ignore','ignore','ignore']`, so that sidecar holds no fd on `.claude/cam-supervisor.log`. The new process-identity check in `defaultListProcesses` (src/commands/stop.ts:449-453) requires exactly that open fd, so a liveness-watch-respawned sidecar is invisible to `cam stop`'s fallback scoped scan and is silently left running in the one situation the fallback exists for (pid file absent or stale, e.g. after an earlier `cam stop` removed the pid file without the SIGTERM taking). main matched this class via `argv[0] === 'cam'`, so it is a regression. Reviewer's independent probe against the real ps+lsof production path (scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3): pid A (spawnSidecarDefault shape, holds the log open) matched and was SIGTERM'd; pid B (byte-for-byte the makeSpawnSidecarFn shape) matched=false. This also falsifies the universal invariant the identity check is justified by, asserted at src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts:20-27 ('Every real sidecar process holds this file open on fd 1/2 for its entire lifetime') and repeated at src/commands/stop.ts:403-406, and the decoy case in test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts:89-92 codifies that exact production shape as a process that must NOT be matched. Mechanical 2-file fix: give the respawn the same `openSync(join(cwd,'.claude',SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME),'a')` stdout/stderr redirection `spawnSidecarDefault` uses (src/commands/run.ts:856-860; Bun docs confirm a raw fd number is a supported stdout/stderr value), plus a regression case in test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts asserting a liveness-watch-shaped respawn IS discovered.

Carried from rounds 1-3 and still unaddressed: `bootstrapHub` has no injectable spawnSync seam, so its exit-status mapping ((result.status ?? 1) === 0, including the signal-killed null case) has zero direct coverage, and the `if (cmd === undefined) return false` guard at line 42 is an unreachable branch that exists only to satisfy noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Injecting a spawnSync fn (as stop.ts already does with spawnSyncFn) makes the mapping testable and removes the dead branch. This is a new shared file, so the seam is cheaper to add now than after six proxies depend on it.

`parseLsofOpenFiles` has no direct unit test: its edge cases (an `n` line with no preceding `f` line, output with no `cwd` entry, trailing blank lines, a name containing whitespace) are only exercised indirectly through the real-lsof integration test, which cannot produce malformed input. A small pure-function test over fixture lsof text would give the parser its own error/edge triad without any I/O.

`expectedLogPath` is built as `join(cwd, '.claude', SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME)` from the lsof-reported (realpath-resolved) cwd and compared with `===` against lsof's reported open-file names. If `.claude/` (or the log file itself) is a symlink, or the log has been rotated out from under the process, lsof reports the resolved/other path and the identity check misses a genuine sidecar. A `realpathSync`-tolerant comparison (or matching on basename plus the cwd prefix) would remove that sharp edge.

Residual stale cross-references in the knowledge layer (the US-R2-002 bullet corrects the argv[0] anchor but not these): (a) the US-R1-003 bullet still states the production default does `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid> -F n` cwd resolution, but it is now a single `lsof -p <pid> -F fn` call plus the holdsSidecarLogOpen identity check, and the integration test now spawns three processes, not two; (b) the US-R1-002 bullet points at 'the "[resolved 2026-08-02]" US-004 bullet above', a marker US-R1-004 removed, so the pointer no longer resolves; (c) the US-004 bullet headline still reads 'length 2 or 3', which is no longer the predicate and is what a future grep hits first.

Carried from rounds 1-3: the four one-line self-spawn builders account for the whole +53-line run.ts ceiling raise in scripts/file-size-budget.json (1169 -> 1222). They are pure wrappers over buildSelfSpawnArgv with no run.ts dependency (buildSidecarRespawnArgv in sidecar-liveness-watch.ts is a fifth copy of the same shape); co-locating them in src/util/self-invoke.ts would avoid growing an already 1200-line file. The raise is documented in the _ref tracker, so this is not blocking.

`isSidecarArgv` now carries a 55-line docstring (lines 286-341) over a 3-line body, most of it a chronological narrative of the US-R1-001 anchor being added and then dropped. That narrative is already captured verbatim in patterns.md and the _ref tracker; a short statement of the current contract plus a pointer would keep the same knowledge and recover a large share of the stop.ts 689 -> 799 ceiling raise.
